items.title: Tariffs are back as Anthropic sinks further below its IPO price
items.summary: The 8:30 hosts Julie Hyman and Jake Conley, joined on the couch by BD8 Capital Partners CEO and CIO Barbara Doran, tackle the top stories of the day. Including the Trump administration's sweeping new Section 301 tariffs of 20% on China and dozens of other economies, in-line PCE inflation and a third-quarter GDP revision up to 4.3% that keep a December Fed hike in play, Anthropic sliding toward $78 and well below its $83 IPO price, and whether Jensen Huang is the right leader for Nvidia in a new regulatory era.

items.title: Ten reasons the market is selling off again before Thanksgiving
items.summary: Sozzi Unleashed host Brian Sozzi runs through his list of 10 reasons stocks are selling off again two days after the Jensen Huang relief rally, from a hot PCE report and a possible December Fed hike to new tariffs of up to 20% on China and the EU, and five reasons Nvidia is back under pressure. He questions why Wall Street is shrugging off blowout quarters from Dell and HPE, with HPE CEO Antonio Neri weighing in on server pricing and why the company won't finance neoclouds. Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives joins to argue the selloff is a growth scare, not a bubble, puts fair value on Anthropic as it trades below its IPO price, and previews Huang's testimony in Washington. Brian closes with Walmart's CFO on turkey sales, a look at retail stocks as gas prices fall for 31 straight days, and a Thanksgiving message to investors.

items.title: Dell crushes earnings estimates. Why is the atock falling?
items.summary:
Dell (DELL) topped Wall Street's earnings expectations, reporting revenue of $54.9 billion versus estimates of $49.3 billion and earnings per share of $9.45 versus the expected $6.57. Despite the strong results, Dell shares remain under pressure, down 36% over the past month.

Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi breaks down the disconnect between Dell's financial performance and its stock price, highlighting what Wall Street may be overlooking.

items.title: Nvidia stops shipping AI servers to 4 Southeast Asian countries- FT

items.title: Dell Technologies (DELL) Q3 Earnings Showcase AI Strength Without Stock Heat
items.summary: Dell Technologies walked into this Q3 2027 print with a bruised chart, down sharply over the past one and three months, yet the stock barely budged today, up about 0.6%. That muted move sits awkwardly against a quarter where infrastructure revenue reached US$54.9b and non GAAP earnings per share hit US$9.45, both tied directly to heavy spending on artificial intelligence servers and storage. For you as an investor, the key question is whether the modest price reaction reflects cool judgment...
